fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled RLE packet header byte read from the truncated input file; the high bit (c & 0x80) selects the RLE-pixel branch and count=(c&0x7f)+1 sets the run length.

Root cause: the return value of readRawData is not checked. The stream ends before pixel_size bytes are available, so fewer bytes are read and the remaining bytes of the stack buffer pixel[8] keep uninitialized stack contents instead of being zeroed (unlike the palette/non-RLE paths which check dataRead and memset the tail).
The uninitialized remainder of pixel is copied verbatim into the malloc'd image buffer, propagating the uninitialized bytes into the decoded image.

Sink: the conversion loop reads src[0..3] (and computes alpha from src[3]) from the image buffer that received the uninitialized bytes, feeding uninitialized memory into the output QRgb pixel, which is later consumed (sanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value).

relation.right: pixel buffer contents copied via memcpy

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: Truncated RLE TGA input: packet header claims an RLE run, but the stream ends before pixel_size bytes of pixel data are present; readRawData returns fewer bytes and the unchecked remainder of the stack pixel buffer is copied into the image, so the entire pixel_size worth of 'pixel' does not always contain valid data (either read from the file or explicitly zeroed), and uninitialized memory is read in the conversion loop.
